s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dyspnea with signs of heart failure and preserved ejection fraction
salient_findings: Systolic murmur at the aortic and mitral areas
Pulmonary congestion and pleural effusion on chest radiography
key_facts: 53-year-old man
History of congenital ventricular septal defect repaired in childhood
Aortic valve and septal patch replacements
Permanent atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation
Chronic hepatitis C–related liver disease
Prior admission for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Jugular venous distension on examination
Irregular rhythm on examination
2/6 systolic murmur at the aortic and mitral areas on examination
Decreased breath sounds at the right lung base on examination
Peripheral edema on examination
Atrial fibrillation with left bundle branch block on ECG
Pulmonary congestion and right basal pleural effusion on chest radiography
Dilated left ventricle with preserved ejection fraction on transthoracic echocardiography
Dilated right ventricle with normal systolic function on transthoracic echocardiography
Severe prosthesis–patient mismatch with elevated transprosthetic gradients
Moderate mitral regurgitation on transthoracic echocardiography
Severe tricuspid regurgitation on transthoracic echocardiography
Estimated systolic pulmonary artery pressure of 50 mmHg on transthoracic echocardiography
